column3: “Both love and hatred man does not know; everything is before them” is rendered “Man does not know whether it will be love or hatred; anything awaits him.”
Close to the Hebrew; Like the Hebrew, NASB has no “and to the evil” (a Septuagint addition). “One who fears an oath” is rendered “the one who is afraid to swear.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Madness” is rendered “insanity,” and NASB adds “they go” (“Afterwards they go to the dead”).
Close to the Hebrew; “Envy” is rendered “zeal,” and “portion” as “share.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Food” is rendered “bread,” and “has taken pleasure in” as “has … approved.”
“See life” is rendered “Enjoy life,” and “the days of your life of futility” as “your fleeting life”; NASB does not repeat the second “all the days of your futility.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “verily,” “with your strength” is rendered “with all your might,” and “explanation” as “planning.”
Close to the Hebrew; “The mighty” is rendered “the warriors,” “the knowledgeable” as “men of ability,” and “happens to” as “overtake.”
Close to the Hebrew; “An evil net” is rendered “a treacherous net.”
Close to the Hebrew; “I have seen wisdom” is rendered “I came to see as wisdom,” and “it was great to me” as “it impressed me.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Someone found” is rendered “there was found.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB quotes only the first clause as speech.
Close to the Hebrew; “Cry” is rendered “shouting.”
